messages.subject: Problems with schedule
parts:
I would like to simulate a production line. This line consists of several machines that are run through one after the other. The run lasts more than one day, but there is no production at night.
I have already tried the schedule function, but no order runs through the whole line, because the orders are thrown out of the system every time the capacity of a machine goes to 0. But the orders should stay where they are on the line until the next day and then continue.
Is there a way to simulate this in with simmer?

Is my question clear?

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Problems with schedule
parts:
There was a discussion in this list about this kind of pattern in [1].
I don't remember the specifics, but yes, it's possible. And we even
came to the concept of "interleaved resources", that was implemented
as an add-on in simmer.bricks [2]:

"This brick encapsulates a chain of interleaved resources, i.e., the
current resource is not released until the next one in the chain is
available. An interesting property of such a pattern is that, if one
resource is blocked for some reason, the whole chain stops."

[1] https://groups.google.com/d/msg/simmer-devel/_eLoVGIi5tg/m2GjogkxDAAJ
[2] https://r-simmer.org/extensions/bricks/reference/interleave.html

Iñaki
